tasks.title: Add IsReady and NextTask to afspec and use NextTask in examples/tasks
steps: Write TS-10-1..TS-10-8 (unit tests in afspec/task_test.go, a property test for TS-10-8 using math/rand or testing/quick over generated plans with random states and present/absent/empty/dangling depends_on, and the pick test in examples/tasks/main_test.go) and confirm they fail

Add (*TasksV2Json).IsReady(id int) bool to afspec/task.go: nil receiver or unknown id gives false; task must be pending; dependencies are DependsOn when non-nil (an explicit empty slice means none), otherwise the task immediately before it in plan order (none for the first task); each dependency must exist in the plan and be done (dropped or missing counts as not done)

Add (*TasksV2Json).NextTask() (*Task, bool) beside GetTask: nil receiver or empty plan gives nil,false; return a deep copy (copy DependsOn and other slices and pointers, as GetTask does) of the first in_progress task, otherwise of the first task with IsReady true, otherwise nil,false

Rewrite pick in examples/tasks/main.go so that id 0 uses NextTask; when it returns false keep the two distinct errors: "every task is done or dropped" if every task is done or dropped, else "no pending task has all its dependencies done"; keep the explicit-id path unchanged
Run the existing examples/tasks tests and confirm they pass unchanged

tasks.title: Add AdminResult, AdminEnvelope, DecodeSpeca, TaskCounts, PackageInfo and TaskInfo.ready to envelope
steps: Write TS-10-51..TS-10-54 in envelope/ (marshal each form of AdminResult, reflect over struct tags for description, DecodeSpeca on captured outputs and on "not json", an import check that parses envelope/*.go with go/parser and asserts only standard-library imports) and confirm they fail
Add `Ready bool` to TaskInfo in envelope/render_result.go with json tag `ready,omitempty` and a description tag

Add TaskCounts{Pending, InProgress, Done, Dropped, Total} (json pending, in_progress, done, dropped, total) and PackageInfo{SpecDir, SpecID, SpecName, Title, Status, Valid *bool, TaskCounts *TaskCounts, NextTask *TaskInfo, Archived bool, LoadError string} with omitempty tags so a failed entry holds only spec_dir and load_error, in a new envelope/admin_result.go

Add AdminResult in the same file: identity fields (spec_dir, spec_id, spec_name, title, status, created_at, updated_at, intent_hash, supersedes, tags), Valid *bool, FailingRules, IntentDrift bool omitempty, Tasks/AllowedStatus/DependsOn/Packages with omitzero (so they show as [] only when non-nil empty in their own form), TaskCounts *TaskCounts, NextTask *TaskInfo, Dependents with omitzero, Validation *ValidationReport, Traceability *TraceReport; every field gets a description tag
Make sure empty non-nil slices still marshal as [] with omitzero and nil slices are omitted
Add `type AdminEnvelope = Envelope[*AdminResult]` and `func DecodeSpeca(data []byte) (AdminEnvelope, error)` in envelope/envelope.go modelled on DecodeSpecr
Run the existing envelope tests and confirm they pass unchanged

tasks.title: Create internal/specpkg with the resolver, listing, display rule, task summary and report converters
steps: Before moving anything, capture the JSON of spec's validation and traceability report for a fixture package (errors, warnings, uncovered criteria, an unowned test) as a golden file under internal/specpkg/testdata
Write TS-10-9..TS-10-14 in internal/specpkg and confirm they fail

Create internal/specpkg/locate.go by moving locate, pathCandidates, isSpecDir, specDirs, matching, sameNumber and listed from cmd/specr/locate.go; export Locate(tool, ref, root, specsDir string) (string, error) and List(root string) ([]string, error); keep behaviour identical but build the three refusal messages for -, a URL and a multi-line reference with the tool name passed in (message begins with the tool name); all errors stay cli.Usagef

Add Display(dir, root string) string (the displayPath rule from cmd/specr/main.go) and Rules([]afspec.ValidationEntry) []string-compatible helper (the distinct Check or Category in first-appearance order; keep the string-joining variant that specr needs as a thin wrapper if useful)

Add TaskInfos(spec *afspec.Spec) []envelope.TaskInfo and TaskInfo(plan, task) moved from cmd/specr/render.go: one entry per task in plan order, DependsOn copied, Optional via IsOptional, Ready from plan.IsReady(id); a spec without tasks gives an empty non-nil slice

Move reportOf, itemOf, traceOf and unownedTests from specgen/pipeline.go into internal/specpkg as exported ReportOf, TraceOf (and unexported helpers) returning envelope.ValidationReport and envelope.TraceReport; update specgen/pipeline.go (~lines 897-899) to call them and delete the private copies
Run the specgen tests and confirm spec's result JSON is byte-for-byte equal to the golden
Do not touch cmd/specr yet; it keeps compiling against its own copies until the next task

tasks.title: Switch specr to the shared specpkg code and regenerate its schema golden
steps: Write TS-10-15 in cmd/specr/main_test.go: render package 09 and --task N and assert every pending, ready-dependency task carries ready, and other fields are unchanged; confirm it fails
Delete cmd/specr/locate.go and call specpkg.Locate("specr", ...) from specr's main
Replace specr's displayPath, rules and taskInfos/taskInfo with the specpkg equivalents, keeping the output otherwise identical
Regenerate cmd/specr/testdata/schema.golden.json with UPDATE_GOLEN=1 (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./cmd/specr -run Schema) and review that the only diff is `ready` on TaskInfo
Run all cmd/specr tests and confirm they pass; remove any specr tests that tested the deleted private functions by moving their cases into internal/specpkg

tasks.title: Build the speca command shell: flags, help, version, schema and usage errors
steps: Write TS-10-17..TS-10-21 and TS-10-56 in cmd/speca (main_test.go, schema_test.go modelled on cmd/specr) with a newRepo helper copying afspec/testdata/v2_example to .specs/09_agent_mode and valid_spec_with_arch to .specs/01_test_feature, and a run helper decoding with envelope.DecodeSpeca; confirm they fail

Create cmd/speca/main.go modelled on cmd/specr/main.go: const tool = "speca", Main(argv, stdout, stderr) int, a flag set with --validate, --list, --all, --specs-dir, --dir, --schema, --version, help on stderr whose first lines include the sentence "spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports its state" plus the forms and examples

Parse with cli.SplitArgs; implement -h/--help (exit 0, stdout empty), --version ("speca "+identity), bare invocation (no positional and not --list: print help, exit 2, and emit a usage envelope when stdout is not a terminal)

Implement the usage-error checks before reading anything: more than one input, input with --list, --validate with --list, --all without --list, `-`/URL/multi-line input, --dir not a directory, undefined flag; resolve the reference with specpkg.Locate("speca", ...); print the message to stderr and emit an envelope with stage usage, category usage via a usageInfo helper

Implement the --schema self-description (tool, description containing the sibling sentence, input with examples, flags from cli.FlagsDocument, result from cli.EnvelopeDocument(Result{}, "side_effects","input","model","usage"), exit_codes) behind an injectable encoder variable; on encode failure emit an envelope with stage schema, category internal, exit 1; add the golden test with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and check in cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json
Create cmd/speca/result.go with `type Result struct{ envelope.AdminResult }` and Summary() string and Next() []cli.Next methods that for now return "" and nil (implemented in the next task)

Add a dispatch function execute that selects the report, verdict or list form and calls form functions (report, verdict, list) in separate files; give each a minimal implementation that returns a load-stage failure "form not yet implemented" so the package compiles; tasks 7-9 replace them
Run the tests and confirm they pass

tasks.title: Implement speca's summary and next suggestions
steps: Write TS-10-45..TS-10-50 and TS-10-55 in cmd/speca/result_test.go and confirm they fail; the TS-10-55 test builds Run.Envelope envelopes for each form and error stage and asserts retryable and resumable are false and that Result embeds envelope.AdminResult

Implement Result.Summary(): report form "speca: <dir name> <status>, D of T tasks done[; next task N]" with a does-not-validate clause when valid is false; validate form "speca: <dir> validates" or "speca: <dir> does not validate (N errors: rule, rule)" using the rule names of validation errors; list form "speca: N packages (2 draft, 5 active, ...)" with non-zero status counts in lifecycle order and an "unreadable" count when non-zero; detect the form from which fields are set (Packages non-nil means list, Validation non-nil means validate)

Implement Result.Next(): report with NextTask N gives one cli.Next{Tool: "specr", Input: spec_dir, Flags: --task N, Why: in progress or next ready task}; list gives one entry for the first active package (list order, not archived) with no in_progress task and a ready task, using its next_task id; validate and every other case return nil
Make sure nothing in the result sets Resumable/Retryable true, and the 200-rune cap is applied by Run.Envelope

tasks.title: Implement the speca report form
steps: Write TS-10-24..TS-10-32 in cmd/speca (integration tests over Main with fixture repos built in t.TempDir; TS-10-30 as a property test over generated task plans) and confirm they fail
Implement report in cmd/speca: afspec.LoadSpec on the resolved dir; on error return a failure at stage load, category input, message naming the directory and the library's reason, result absent

Fill identity fields (spec_dir via specpkg.Display, spec_id, spec_name, title, status, created_at, updated_at, intent_hash when set, supersedes and tags when non-empty), valid from Validate always present and failing_rules via specpkg rule names only when invalid

Add a shared helper intentDrift(spec) used by report and verdict: true when status is active, IntentHash set, and ComputeIntentHash(PRDBody) errors or differs; otherwise leave false so the field is omitted

Fill tasks via specpkg.TaskInfos (empty non-nil list for no tasks), task_counts (total equal to len(tasks)), next_task via NextTask converted to TaskInfo, allowed_status from afspec.ValidTransition over draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived in that order (non-nil empty for terminal status)

Fill depends_on from the package's own tasks.json dependencies (file order, de-duplicated, non-nil empty) and dependents via afspec.DiscoverSpecs and BuildDependencyGraph over the spec root (sorted, de-duplicated; use the partial graph despite a dangling dependency error); when the root cannot be read leave dependents nil and call run.Warn(cli.WarnSpecsDirUnreadable, "low", ...) naming the root

Add the legacy-format check shared with specr: when SchemaVersion is neither 0 nor afspec.SchemaVersion raise run.Warn(cli.WarnSpecInvalid, "high", ...) saying tests and tasks are not read; raise no spec_invalid warning for an invalid v2 package
Run the tests and confirm they pass

tasks.title: Implement the speca --validate verdict form
steps: Write TS-10-33..TS-10-39 in cmd/speca/verdict_test.go (fixture roots with packages A, B, C, D, an archived target, a malformed sibling, a v1 package) and confirm they fail

Implement verdict in cmd/speca/verdict.go: load the target (same load failure and legacy-format warning as the report), fill identity fields and intent_drift, and omit tasks, task_counts, next_task, allowed_status, depends_on, dependents and failing_rules

Compute the package's own result with Validate; list the spec root with afspec.DiscoverSpecs semantics but load every NN_name directory with LoadSpec (skip those that fail), and add the target when it is not among them (compare Dir after absolutising, e.g. an archived package); build metas, BuildDependencyGraph (ignore its dangling-reference error) and call afspec.ValidateCrossSpec

Keep from the cross-spec result only errors whose EntityID is the package's spec_id, errors with no entity when the graph has at least one edge from or to the package, and warnings whose EntityID is a term in the package's glossary; append them after the package's own errors and warnings
Convert with specpkg.ReportOf (valid false when any error kept), set result.valid from the same value, and set traceability via specpkg.TraceOf; an invalid package exits 0
When the spec root cannot be read skip the cross-spec rules, raise the low specs_dir_unreadable warning naming the root, and report the own verdict alone
Run the tests and confirm they pass

tasks.title: Implement the speca --list form and its no-write guarantee
steps: Write TS-10-16, TS-10-22 and TS-10-40..TS-10-44 in cmd/speca/list_test.go and main_test.go and confirm they fail; TS-10-22 snapshots the file tree and modification times, sets invalid credential and model environment variables with t.Setenv, and runs every form

Implement list in cmd/speca/list.go: read the root with specpkg.List (not DiscoverSpecs); when the root is missing or unreadable fail at stage load, category input, with a message naming the root and fix hint flag --specs-dir; an existing empty root gives a non-nil empty packages list

Sort directories by numeric prefix compared as a number, ties by full name; load each with LoadSpec; a loaded package gives PackageInfo with spec_dir, spec_id, spec_name, title, status, valid from Validate, task_counts and next_task; a failure gives an entry with only spec_dir and load_error and the call continues
With --all append the directories under <root>/archive/ in the same order each with archived true regardless of status; a missing archive/ adds nothing and no warning
Confirm speca's code calls no os.Create/WriteFile/Mkdir/Rename and reads no environment variable, and that nothing in the call path touches the network
Run the tests, including TS-10-16 across all forms and flag orders, and confirm they pass

tasks.title: Install speca in the build and update documentation and the ADR
steps: Write TS-10-23 (a test that runs `make -n build` with os/exec and counts the three -ldflags installs, the ./cmd/speca path and the help line) and confirm it fails
Update the Makefile build target to install ./cmd/speca with $(LDFLAGS) beside ./cmd/spec and ./cmd/specr, and its help line to name all three
Create docs/speca.md modelled on docs/specr.md: forms, input, report, output, errors, warnings, flags, --schema and calling it from an agent

Update README.md (a speca section; correct the "no CLI surface" sentence to say reading state has a command while changing it is still library API), docs/architecture.md (layout with cmd/speca and internal/specpkg, a section on the speca command with its package graph, the Consumers paragraph), docs/api.md (AdminResult, AdminEnvelope, DecodeSpeca, PackageInfo, TaskCounts, TaskInfo.ready), docs/specr.md (ready in task fields), afspec/README.md (IsReady and NextTask)
Write docs/adr/10-report-and-change-the-state-of-a-package-with-its-own-command.md recording the decision to build speca, modelled on ADR 05
Run `make doc` to regenerate docs/generated (including docs/generated/cmd/speca.txt); write no test that checks doc content

tasks.title: Verify the speca execution paths end to end
steps: Write TS-10-57..TS-10-60 as smoke tests in cmd/speca/smoke_test.go against the real speca and specr Main entry points and real fixtures on disk, and confirm they pass

Trace 10-PATH-1 to 10-PATH-4 through the real code: Main, cli.SplitArgs, specpkg.Locate, afspec.LoadSpec, Validate, IsReady, NextTask, ValidTransition, DiscoverSpecs, BuildDependencyGraph, ValidateCrossSpec, specpkg converters, Run.Envelope and Emit; confirm each step calls the next and no placeholder form function remains in cmd/speca/forms.go

Confirm producers are consumed in production code: IsReady and NextTask by specpkg.TaskInfos, specr, speca and examples/tasks; specpkg.Locate, Display and TaskInfos by specr and speca; specpkg.ReportOf and TraceOf by specgen and speca; envelope.DecodeSpeca by tests only is acceptable as a public API

Search every file listed in the tasks' touches (afspec/task.go, examples/tasks, envelope, internal/specpkg, specgen/pipeline.go, cmd/specr, cmd/speca) for TODO, panic("not implemented"), "not yet implemented" and bare `return nil` on non-trivial paths, and remove any that remain
Run make test and make lint, and run make doc so docs/generated is current
